pairs.fullEnglish: Judah drew near to him and said, ‘Please, my lord, let your servant now speak a word before my lord, and do not let your anger grow strong against your servant, for you are like Pharaoh.’
‘My lord asked his servants, saying, “Do you have a father or a brother?”’
‘We said to my lord, “We have an aged father and a young son of his old age. His brother is dead, and he alone remains of his mother, and his father loves him.”’
‘You said to your servants, “Bring him down to me, and I will set my eye upon him.”’
‘You said to your servants, “If your youngest brother does not come down with you, you shall not see my face again.”’
‘When we went up to your servant, my father, we told him my lord’s words.’
‘Our father said, “Go back; buy us a little grain.”’
‘We said, “We cannot go down. If our youngest brother is with us, we will go down, for we cannot see the man’s face when our youngest brother is not with us.”’
‘Your servant, my father, said to us, “You know that my wife bore me two sons.”’
‘“One went away from me, and I said, ‘Surely he has been killed,’ and I have not seen him until now.”’
‘“If you take this one too away from before me, and death befalls him, you will bring my gray hair down in misery to the grave.”’
‘And now, when I come to your servant, my father, and the youth is not with us—his life is as dear to him as his own life—’
‘When he sees that the youth is not there, he will die, and your servants will bring the gray hair of your servant, our father, down in sorrow to the grave.’
‘For your servant became surety for the youth to my father, saying, “If I do not bring him to you, I shall be guilty before my father for all time.”’
‘For how can I go up to my father when the youth is not with me, lest I see the misery that will overtake my father?’
Joseph could not restrain himself before all those standing about him, and he called out, ‘Send everyone away from me!’ No one remained with him when Joseph made himself known to his brothers.
He raised his voice in weeping, and the Egyptians heard, and the people of Pharaoh’s household heard.
Joseph said to his brothers, ‘I am Joseph. Is my father still alive?’ His brothers could not answer him a word, for they were dismayed before him.
Joseph said to his brothers, ‘Come near to me now.’ They came near, and he said, ‘I am Joseph, your brother, whom you sold into Egypt.’
‘And now, do not be distressed, and do not let it be grievous in your eyes that you sold me here, for יְיָ sent me ahead of you to preserve life.’
‘For these have been two years of famine within the land, and there are still five years in which there will be neither sowing nor harvest.’
‘יְיָ sent me ahead of you to establish a remnant for you in the land and to keep you alive for a great deliverance.’
‘And now, it was not you who sent me here, but it was from before יְיָ. He made me a father to Pharaoh, lord over all the people of his household, and ruler over all the land of Egypt.’
‘Hurry and go up to my father, and say to him, “Thus says your son Joseph: יְיָ has made me lord over all Egypt. Come down to me; do not delay.”’
‘“You shall dwell in the land of Goshen and be near me—you, your sons, your sons’ sons, your flocks, your cattle, and all that is yours.”’
‘“I will sustain you there, for there are still five years of famine, lest you become impoverished—you, the people of your household, and all that is yours.”’
‘Look, your eyes see, and the eyes of my brother Benjamin, that I am speaking with you in your own language.’
‘Tell my father of all my honor in Egypt and of everything you have seen. Hurry and bring my father down here.’
He fell upon the neck of his brother Benjamin and wept, and Benjamin wept upon his neck.
He kissed all his brothers and wept over them, and afterward his brothers spoke with him.
The report was heard in Pharaoh’s household, saying, ‘Joseph’s brothers have come.’ It was pleasing in Pharaoh’s eyes and in the eyes of his servants.
Pharaoh said to Joseph, ‘Say to your brothers, “Do this: load your beasts, and go, convey the loads to the land of Canaan.”’
‘“Bring your father and the people of your households, and come to me. I will give you the good of the land of Egypt, and you shall eat the bounty of the land.”’
‘And you are commanded: “Do this: take wagons for yourselves from the land of Egypt for your little ones and your wives, and carry your father and come.”’
‘“Let your eye not have pity on your belongings, for the best of all the land of Egypt is yours.”’
The sons of Israel did so. Joseph gave them wagons at Pharaoh’s command and gave them provisions for the journey.
To his father he sent the following: ten male donkeys laden with the bounty of Egypt and ten female donkeys laden with grain, bread, and provisions for his father for the journey.
He sent his brothers away, and they went. He said to them, ‘Do not quarrel on the journey.’
They went up from Egypt and came to the land of Canaan, to their father Jacob.
They spoke to him all the words that Joseph had spoken with them. He saw the wagons Joseph had sent to carry him, and a spirit of prophecy rested upon their father Jacob.
Israel said, ‘Great is my joy! My son Joseph is still alive. I will go and see him before I die.’
יְיָ spoke to Israel in visions of the night and said, ‘Jacob, Jacob!’ He said, ‘Here I am.’
‘I will go down with you to Egypt, and I will surely bring you up again, and Joseph shall place his hands upon your eyes.’
Jacob arose from בְּאֵרָא דְשָׁבַע, and the sons of Israel carried their father Jacob, their little ones, and their wives in the wagons Pharaoh had sent to carry him.
They brought their livestock and their possessions that they had acquired in the land of Canaan, and they came to Egypt—Jacob and all his sons with him.
His sons and his sons’ sons with him, his daughters and his sons’ daughters, and all his offspring he brought with him into Egypt.
These are the names of the sons of Israel who came into Egypt—Jacob and his sons: Jacob’s firstborn was Reuben.
The sons of Reuben were חֲנוֹךְ, פַלּוּא, חֶצְרֹן, and כַרְמִי.
The sons of Simeon were יְמוּאֵל, יָמִין, אֹהַד, יָכִין, צֹחַר, and שָׁאוּל, the son of the Canaanite woman.
The sons of Levi were גֵּרְשׁוֹן, קְהָת, and מְרָרִי.
The sons of Judah were עֵר, אוֹנָן, שֵׁלָה, פֶרֶץ, and זָרַח. עֵר and אוֹנָן died in the land of Canaan, and the sons of פֶרֶץ were חֶצְרֹן and חָמוּל.
The sons of יִשָּׂשׂכָר were תּוֹלָע, פֻוָּה, יוֹב, and שִׁמְרוֹן.
The sons of זְבֻלוּן were סֶרֶד, אֵלוֹן, and יַחְלְאֵל.
These are the sons of Leah whom she bore to Jacob in פַּדַּן אֲרָם, and Dinah his daughter. All the persons of his sons and daughters were thirty-three.
The sons of Gad were צִפְיוֹן, חַגִּי, שׁוּנִי, אֶצְבּוֹן, עֵרִי, אֲרוֹדִי, and אַרְאֵלִי.
The sons of Asher were יִמְנָה, יִשְׁוָה, יִשְׁוִי, and בְרִיעָה, and שֶׂרַח was their sister. The sons of בְרִיעָה were חֶבֶר and מַלְכִּיאֵל.
These are the sons of Zilpah, whom Laban gave to his daughter Leah. She bore these to Jacob—sixteen persons.
The sons of Rachel, Jacob’s wife, were Joseph and Benjamin.
To Joseph in the land of Egypt were born מְנַשֶּׁה and אֶפְרָיִם, whom אָסְנַת, daughter of פּוֹטִי פֶרַע, chief of אוֹן, bore to him.
The sons of Benjamin were בֶּלַע, בֶכֶר, אַשְׁבֵּל, גֵּרָא, נַעֲמָן, אֵחִי, רֹאשׁ, מֻפִּים, חֻפִּים, and אָרְדְּ.
These are the sons of Rachel who were born to Jacob—all the persons were fourteen.
The sons of Dan: חֻשִׁים.
The sons of Naphtali were יַחְצְאֵל, גוּנִי, יֵצֶר, and שִׁלֵּם.
These are the sons of Bilhah, whom Laban gave to his daughter Rachel. She bore these to Jacob—all the persons were seven.
All the persons who came with Jacob into Egypt, those who issued from his loins, apart from the wives of Jacob’s sons—all the persons were sixty-six.
Joseph’s sons who were born to him in Egypt were two persons. All the persons of Jacob’s household who came into Egypt were seventy.
He sent Judah ahead of him to Joseph, to clear the way ahead of him to Goshen, and they came to the land of Goshen.
Joseph readied his chariot and went up to meet his father Israel in Goshen. He appeared to him, fell upon his neck, and continued weeping upon his neck.
Israel said to Joseph, ‘If I were to die at this time, I would be comforted, after seeing your face, for you are still alive.’
Joseph said to his brothers and his father’s household, ‘I will go up and tell Pharaoh, and say to him, “My brothers and my father’s household, who were in the land of Canaan, have come to me.”’
‘“The men are shepherds of flocks, for they have been men who own livestock, and they have brought their flocks, their cattle, and all that is theirs.”’
‘When Pharaoh calls you and says, “What is your occupation?”’

‘You shall say, “Your servants have been men who own livestock from our youth until now, both we and our fathers,” so that you may dwell in the land of Goshen, for the Egyptians shun all shepherds of flocks.’
Joseph came and told Pharaoh, saying, ‘My father and my brothers, their flocks, their cattle, and all that is theirs have come from the land of Canaan, and here they are in the land of Goshen.’
From among his brothers he took five men and presented them before Pharaoh.
Pharaoh said to his brothers, ‘What is your occupation?’ They said to Pharaoh, ‘Your servants are shepherds of flocks, both we and our fathers.’
Pharaoh said to Joseph, ‘Your father and your brothers have come to you.’

‘The land of Egypt is before you. Settle your father and your brothers in the best of the land; let them dwell in the land of Goshen. If you know that there are able men among them, appoint them as overseers of livestock over what is mine.’
Joseph brought his father Jacob and presented him before Pharaoh, and Jacob blessed Pharaoh.
Pharaoh said to Jacob, ‘How many are the days of the years of your life?’

Jacob said to Pharaoh, ‘The days of the years of my sojourning are a hundred and thirty years. Few and bad have been the days of the years of my life, and they have not reached the days of the years of my fathers’ lives in the days of their sojourning.’
Jacob blessed Pharaoh and went out from before Pharaoh.
Joseph settled his father and his brothers and gave them a possession in the land of Egypt, in the best of the land, in the land of רַעְמְּסֵס, as Pharaoh had commanded.
Joseph sustained his father, his brothers, and all his father’s household with bread, according to the little ones.
There was no bread in all the land, for the famine was exceedingly severe. The people of the land of Egypt and the people of the land of Canaan were exhausted because of the famine.
Joseph gathered all the money that was found in the land of Egypt and in the land of Canaan in exchange for the grain they were buying, and Joseph brought the money to Pharaoh’s house.
The money was exhausted from the land of Egypt and from the land of Canaan, and all the Egyptians came to Joseph, saying, ‘Give us bread. Why should we die before you, for the money is exhausted?’
Joseph said, ‘Give your livestock, and I will give to you in exchange for your livestock, if the money is exhausted.’

They brought their livestock to Joseph, and Joseph gave them bread in exchange for the horses, the flocks of sheep and goats, the herds of cattle, and the donkeys. He sustained them with bread in exchange for all their livestock during that year.

That year ended, and they came to him in the second year and said to him, ‘We will not conceal it from my lord. Rather, the money is exhausted, and the livestock is with my lord. Nothing remains before my lord except our bodies and our land.’

‘Why should we die before your eyes, both we and our land? Buy us and our land in exchange for bread, and we and our land shall be servants to Pharaoh. Give seed grain, so that we may live and not die, and the land may not lie fallow.’
Joseph bought all the land of Egypt for Pharaoh, for the Egyptians sold their fields, each man his own, because the famine was severe upon them, and the land became Pharaoh’s.
As for the people, he transferred them from town to town, from the extremities of the territory of Egypt to its far end.
Only the land of the priests he did not buy, for the priests had an allotted portion from Pharaoh, and they ate their portion that Pharaoh gave them. Therefore they did not sell their land.
Joseph said to the people, ‘Look, I have bought you today and your land for Pharaoh. Here is seed grain for you, and you shall sow the land.’

‘When the produce is brought in, you shall give one part out of five to Pharaoh, and four portions shall be yours for seed grain for the field, for your food, for the people in your households, and for food for your little ones.’
They said, ‘You have kept us alive. May we find favor in my lord’s eyes, and we shall be servants to Pharaoh.’
Joseph established it as a decree, to this day, concerning the land of Egypt, that they should give one part out of five to Pharaoh. Only the land of the priests alone did not become Pharaoh’s.
Israel dwelt in the land of Egypt, in the land of Goshen. They acquired possessions in it, increased, and multiplied exceedingly.
‘And now, please let your servant remain in place of the youth as a servant to my lord, and let the youth go up with his brothers.’
To all of them he gave, to each man, robes of clothing; and to Benjamin he gave three hundred silver units (סִלְעִין) and five robes of clothing.
Israel journeyed with all that was his, came to בְאֵר שָׁבַע, and offered sacrifices to the God of his father Isaac.
He said, ‘I am אֵל, the God of your father. Do not be afraid to go down to Egypt, for I will make you a numerous people there.’

They said to Pharaoh, ‘We have come to sojourn in the land, for there is no pasture for your servants’ flocks, because the famine is severe in the land of Canaan. And now, please let your servants dwell in the land of Goshen.’
‘We said to my lord, “The youth cannot leave his father; and if he leaves his father, he will die.”’

qualifications.he: נושא הפועל ״ומית״ אינו נקוב במילה עצמה. הכינוי ״הוא״ שבאנגלית משאיר פתוח אם הדברים מכוונים לנער או לאביו, ואינו מכריע כאן בזהות המת.
qualifications.en: The subject of וּמִית is not named in the verb itself. The English “he” leaves open whether the youth or his father is meant; it does not resolve that referent here.

pairs.fullEnglish: They told him, saying, ‘Joseph is still alive, and he is ruler over all the land of Egypt.’ But the words left his heart unmoved, for he did not believe them.

qualifications.he: לשון אונקלוס מוסבת על המילים: מִלַּיָּא פָּיְגָן עַל לִבֵּיהּ. ״לא הניעו את לבו״ מביע כאן את חוסר השפעת הדברים בהקשר של אי־האמונה, ולא קובע אבחנה גופנית של הלב.
qualifications.en: Onkelos makes the words the subject: מִלַּיָּא פָּיְגָן עַל לִבֵּיהּ. “Left his heart unmoved” conveys their lack of effect in the context of his disbelief, not a physical diagnosis of his heart.

pairs.fullEnglish: A word of prophecy from before יְיָ was with me, saying:

You, son of man, take one board for yourself and write upon it: For the tribe of יְהוּדָה and the children of יִשְׂרָאֵל, their brothers. Take another board and write upon it: For the tribe of יוֹסֵף, which is the tribe of אֶפְרַיִם, and the whole house of יִשְׂרָאֵל, their brothers.
Bring them near to one another for yourself, to become one board, and they will be as one in your hand.
When the children of your people say to you: Will you not tell us what these things mean for you?

Prophesy to them: Thus says יְיָ אֱלֹהִים: I am bringing near the tribe of יוֹסֵף, which is the tribe of אֶפְרַיִם, and the tribes of יִשְׂרָאֵל, their brothers. I shall join them to it, to the tribe of יְהוּדָה, and make them one people; they will be one before Me.
The boards upon which you write will be in your hand before their eyes.
One who works in summer is a discerning son; one who sleeps at harvest is a son who brings shame.
The remembrance of the righteous is a blessing, but the name of the wicked will be extinguished.
One whose heart is wise will receive a commandment, but a fool is caught by his lips.
One who walks in integrity will go with support; one whose ways are crooked will become known.
One who signals with his eyes causes pain; one who is crooked with his lips is caught.

Prophesy to them: Thus says יְיָ אֱלֹהִים: I am bringing the children of יִשְׂרָאֵל near from among the peoples to which they were exiled. I shall gather them from all around and bring them into their land.

They will no longer become impure through their idols, their abominations, or any of their rebellions. I shall redeem them from all their dwelling places in which they sinned before Me, and purify them. They will be a people before Me, and I shall be their God.
My servant דָוִד will be king over them, and they will all have one leader. They will walk according to My judgments and keep My ordinances and do them.
Hatred stirs up quarrels, but love covers all offenses.
Wisdom is found upon the lips of the discerning, but a rod is for the body of one who lacks understanding.
The wise store up knowledge, but with the mouth of a fool, destruction is near.

They will dwell upon the land that I gave to My servant יַעֲקֹב, in which your fathers dwelt. They, their children and their children’s children will dwell upon it forever; and My servant דָוִד will be their king forever.
I shall establish a covenant of peace for them; it will be an everlasting covenant with them. I shall bless them and increase them, and place My sanctuary among them forever.
I shall cause My Divine Presence to dwell among them. I shall be their God, and they will be a people before Me.
The peoples will know that I am יְיָ Who sanctifies יִשְׂרָאֵל, when My sanctuary is among them forever.
A word of prophecy from before יְיָ was with me, saying:
A rich person’s property is his fortified city; the destruction of the poor is their need.
The deeds of the righteous are for life; the produce of the wicked is for sin.
Those who keep discipline are on the path of life, but one who abandons reproof goes astray.
With an abundance of words, sin does not cease; one who restrains his lips is discerning.
Son of man, receive prophecy concerning גוֹג of the land of מָגוֹג, the chief head of מֶשֶׁךְ and תֻבָל, and prophesy concerning him.
Say: Thus says יְיָ אֱלֹהִים: I am sending My anger upon you, גוֹג, chief head of מֶשֶׁךְ and תֻבָל.
I shall draw you on and place rings upon your jaws, and bring you out with your whole army: horses and horsemen, all fully clothed, many companies armed with bucklers and shields, all holding swords.
The פַּרְסָאֵי, כּוּשְׁאֵי and פּוּטָאֵי will be with them, all armed with bucklers and helmets.
Make ready and prepare yourself, you and all your camps that have gathered about you; be a guard for them.
The lips of the righteous feed many, but fools die for lack of understanding.
The blessing of God makes rich, and pain is not added with it.
As a whirlwind passes, so the wicked will pass; but the righteous is a foundation in the world.
You will go up in tumult; you will come like a rising cloud covering the land—you, your whole army and many peoples with you.
Thus says יְיָ אֱלֹהִים: At that time thoughts will rise in your heart, and you will devise evil plans.

You will say: I shall go up against a land settled in tranquility, in open towns. I shall go against a people who are quiet and all dwell securely, all dwelling without a wall, with neither bars nor gates.
Like vinegar to the teeth and smoke to the eyes, so is a lazy messenger to those who send him.
The fear of God adds days, but the years of the wicked will be shortened.
The hope of the righteous is joy, but the hope of the wicked will perish.
The way of God is a stronghold for the blameless, but destruction will be for those who do iniquity.
The righteous will never be shaken, but the wicked will not be gathered in the land.
One who conceals an enemy has lying lips; one who spreads a report is a fool.

qualifications.he: בעל דבבא הוא אויב או צד עוין; הנוסח אינו מציין אדם מסוים ואינו מפרט מה מוסתר ביחסי העוינות.
qualifications.en: בְּעֵל דְבָבָא denotes an enemy or hostile party. The wording names no particular person and does not further specify what is concealed in that hostile relationship.

pairs.fullEnglish: To plunder plunder and take spoil, to gather your camps against ruins that have been resettled, and against a people gathered from among the peoples who have prospered in possessions and property, dwelling upon the land’s stronghold.

qualifications.he: תוקפא הוא לשון תוקף וחוזק. ״מעוז הארץ״ משמר את הדימוי הזה בלי לזהות מקום מודרני ובלי להמירו אוטומטית ב״טבור הארץ״ שבפסוק העברי.
qualifications.en: תּוּקְפָא expresses strength. 'The land's stronghold' preserves that image without identifying a modern location or automatically replacing it with the Hebrew verse's navel of the land.

pairs.fullEnglish: גוֹמֶר and all her camps, the province of גַרְמַמְיָא at the extremities of the north and all their camps—many peoples will be with you.

qualifications.he: גרממיא הוא שם המקום שבנוסח המסופק. כאן הוא נשמר כשם עתיק, בלי זיהוי עם מדינה מודרנית ובלי קביעת זמן לאירועי הנבואה.
qualifications.en: גַרְמַמְיָא is the place-name in the supplied text. It is retained as an ancient name, without identifying it with a modern country or dating the prophecy's events.

pairs.fullEnglish: I shall make them one people in the land, on the holy mountain of יִשְׂרָאֵל, of יִשְׂרָאֵל. One king will be king over them all. They will no longer be two peoples, and they will never again be divided into two kingdoms.

qualifications.he: בנוסח המסופק דישראל כתוב פעמיים, והחזרה נשמרת גם בתרגום. אין בכך הכרעה כיצד נוצרה החזרה או תיקון של המקור.
qualifications.en: The supplied text writes דְיִשְׂרָאֵל twice, and the translation preserves both occurrences. This does not decide how the repetition arose or amend the original.

pairs.fullEnglish: When a fool laughs, he performs a deed; wisdom belongs to a man of understanding.
The mouth of the righteous is a spring of life, but the mouth of the wicked conceals robbery.

qualifications.he: פּוּמְהוֹן נקרא כנושא הקיבוצי של המשפט, נְכַסָא כפועל פעיל של כיסוי או הסתרה בלשון בעלת תחילית נ־, וחֲטוֹפָא כדבר המוסתר. לכן הפה של הרשעים מסתיר את החטיפה, ולא החטיפה מכסה את פיהם. רש״י על העברית מפרש 'פִּיהֶם יְכַסֶּה חָמָס שֶׁבְּלִבָּם' ומבחין במפורש בין פסוק זה לפסוק י:ו; זו תמיכה עניינית בבחירת התחביר הזמין בארמית, לא ציטוט כתרגומו. אין תוספת בגוף התרגום של חנופה או שנאה שבלב. נשמר הפה בלשון יחיד קיבוצית עם בעלי הפה בלשון רבים.
qualifications.en: פּוּמְהוֹן is read as the clause's collective subject, נְכַסָא as an active covering/concealing verb in n-prefixed usage, and חֲטוֹפָא as what is concealed. Thus the wicked mouth conceals robbery, rather than robbery covering the mouth. Rashi on the Hebrew says 'פִּיהֶם יְכַסֶּה חָמָס שֶׁבְּלִבָּם' and expressly distinguishes this verse from 10:6; this is contextual support for the available Aramaic construction, not a כתרגומו quotation. Flattery and hidden hatred are not added to the body. Singular collective 'mouth' is retained with plural possessors.

pairs.fullEnglish: Blessings will be upon the heads of the righteous; with the mouth of the wicked, he will conceal robbery.

qualifications.he: בקריאה זו נְכַסֵי הוא פועל פעיל של כיסוי או הסתרה בגוף שלישי יחיד, וחֲטוֹפָא הוא הדבר המוסתר, חטיפה או גזל. בי״ת של בְּפוּמְהוֹן מציינת את האמצעי: באמצעות הפה של הרשעים. זהות עושה הפעולה אינה נקובה במשפט; ׳הוא׳ שבתרגום אינו מזהה אותו עם אדם מסוים. פּוּמְהוֹן נשמר כפה קיבוצי שבעליו רבים. אין זו אמירה סבילה שהגזל יוסתר, ולא תוספת של הריגה.
qualifications.en: In this reading נְכַסֵי is an active third-person singular covering/concealing verb, and חֲטוֹפָא is what is concealed, robbery or plunder. The בְּ of בְּפוּמְהוֹן marks the means: with the wicked's mouth. The clause does not name the acting subject; the English ‘he’ does not identify a particular person. פּוּמְהוֹן is retained as a collective singular mouth with plural possessors. This is not a passive statement that robbery will be concealed, and no killing consequence is added.

pairs.fullEnglish: The tongue of the righteous person is choice silver, but the heart of the wicked is deficient.

qualifications.he: מַחֲתָא היא כאן שם עצם במשמעות חיסרון, המשמש נשוא של לב הרשעים; לפיכך נמסר באנגלית שהלב חסר. אין זה פועל של נפילה או הכאה, ואין הכוונה למקומו הגופני של הלב. לִבָּא הוא יחיד המתייחס לרשעים בלשון רבים, כנגד לשונו של הצדיק היחיד בצלע הראשונה. ההשוואה לכסף נבחר אינה קובעת מידה מספרית של ערך ואינה אומרת שלב הרשעים עשוי מתכת או סגסוגת מסוימת.
qualifications.en: מַחֲתָא here is a noun meaning deficiency, used as the predicate of the wicked people's heart; English therefore renders the heart as 'deficient.' It is not a verb of falling or striking, nor a statement about the heart's physical position. לִבָּא is singular and refers collectively to plural wicked people, in contrast with the singular righteous person's tongue in the first clause. The choice-silver comparison supplies neither a numerical degree of worth nor a claim that the wicked heart consists of a metal or a particular alloy.

pairs.fullEnglish: After many days you will muster your army. At the end of years you will go against a land to which people have returned from the slaughters of the sword, gathered from many peoples, upon the mountains of the land of יִשְׂרָאֵל that had been continually desolate. They have come out from among the peoples, and all of them dwell securely.

qualifications.he: הצירוף מופיע בתיאור השבים והמתכנסים מן העמים. אין מוסיפים לו קביעה נפרדת על תחיית המתים.
qualifications.en: The phrase occurs in a description of people returning and gathering from the nations. No separate assertion about resurrection is added.

qualifications.he: מִבֵּינֵי מציין את כיוון היציאה מן העמים; לא נקראו בשם המוציא או אופן היציאה.
qualifications.en: מִבֵּינֵי marks movement out from among the peoples; neither the removing agent nor the manner of departure is named.

pairs.fullEnglish: What is decreed for the wicked will come to him, but the desire of the righteous will be given to them.

qualifications.he: חריצותא היא הקריאה הראשית כאן, ונמסרת במשמעות הדבר הנגזר לרשע. חריינותא ניתנת בסוגריים כאפשרות של כתיב אחר, לא כתיקון ודאי של כל העדים.
qualifications.en: חריצותא is the main reading here, understood as what is decreed for the wicked. חריינותא is shown in parentheses as a possible different spelling, not as a certain correction of every witness.

dayTitle.he: יהודה מציג את דברי האחים ואת תנאי השליט
dayTitle.en: Judah recounts the brothers’ words and the ruler’s condition

explanation.he: יהודה פותח בבקשת רשות לדבר לפני השליט בלי לעורר את כעסו. הוא חוזר על השאלה בדבר האב והאח ועל תיאור אהבת האב לבן שנותר מאמו. הדברים מסתיימים בתנאי שהאח הצעיר יבוא עמם כדי שיוכלו לשוב ולראות את פני השליט.
explanation.en: Judah opens by asking leave to speak before the ruler without provoking his anger. He recalls the question about their father and brother and the account of the father’s love for the son who remains of his mother. The passage ends with the condition that the youngest brother accompany them before they may see the ruler’s face again.

dayTitle.he: הבקשה לשוב לקנות תבואה והצורך באח הצעיר
dayTitle.en: The request for more grain and the need for the youngest brother

explanation.he: יהודה מתאר כיצד מסרו לאביהם את דברי השליט אחרי שעלו אליו. בקשת האב לקנות עוד תבואה נענית בחזרה על התנאי המונע מהם לרדת בלי אחיהם הצעיר. בסיום מתחילים דברי האב על שני הבנים שילדה לו אשתו.
explanation.en: Judah describes how they reported the ruler’s words to their father after going up to him. The father’s request for more grain is met by a restatement of the condition that prevents them from going down without their youngest brother. The closing verse begins the father’s account of the two sons his wife bore him.

dayTitle.he: חיי הנער היקרים לאב וערבות יהודה
dayTitle.en: The youth’s life, dear to his father, and Judah’s surety

explanation.he: בדברי האב המובאים כאן נאמר שהבן שיצא ממנו נהרג, ולא נאמר שנטרף. יהודה מסביר שחיי הנער יקרים לאב כחייו שלו, ולכן שיבה בלעדיו תביא למות האב וליגונו. הוא מוסיף את ערבותו האישית ואת האשמה שיקבל עליו אם לא ישיב את הנער.
explanation.en: In the father’s words quoted here, the son who went away is said to have been killed, not torn by a beast. Judah explains that the youth’s life is as dear to his father as his own, so returning without him would bring the father death and sorrow. He adds his personal surety and the lasting guilt he undertook if he failed to bring the youth back.

dayTitle.he: הצעת יהודה לעבדות וגילוי יוסף לאחיו
dayTitle.en: Judah’s offer of servitude and Joseph’s disclosure to his brothers

explanation.he: יהודה מציע להישאר כעבד במקום הנער, מפני שאינו יכול לשוב לאביו בלעדיו ולראות ברעתו. יוסף מוציא את הנוכחים האחרים ואינו עוצר עוד את בכיו. הוא מציג את עצמו לאחיו ושואל על חיי אביו, ואחר כך מזכיר במפורש שהם מכרו אותו למצרים.
explanation.en: Judah offers to remain as a servant in the youth’s place because he cannot return without him and witness his father’s misery. Joseph sends the other people out and no longer holds back his weeping. He identifies himself to his brothers and asks whether his father is alive, then explicitly recalls that they sold him into Egypt.

dayTitle.he: שליחות יוסף לקיום החיים והקריאה לאביו
dayTitle.en: Joseph’s mission to preserve life and his summons to his father

explanation.he: יוסף אינו משמיט את מכירתו, אך מציג את בואו לפני האחים כשליחות מאת יְיָ לקיומם בשנות הרעב. הוא מונה את השנים שנותרו בלי זריעה וקציר ואת מעמדו בבית פרעה ובמצרים. מתוך כך הוא שולח את האחים להזמין את אביו לרדת אליו בלי להתעכב.
explanation.en: Joseph does not omit the sale, but presents his coming ahead of his brothers as a mission from יְיָ to sustain them during the famine. He specifies the remaining years without sowing or harvest and his position in Pharaoh’s household and in Egypt. He therefore sends the brothers to invite his father to come down without delay.

dayTitle.he: ההזמנה למצרים, רוח הנבואה וההבטחה ליעקב
dayTitle.en: The invitation to Egypt, the spirit of prophecy, and the promise to Jacob

explanation.he: יוסף מבטיח לכלכל את משפחתו בארץ גושן ומדגיש שהוא מדבר עם אחיו בלשונם; פרעה מוסיף עגלות והזמנה ליהנות מטוב מצרים. כשיעקב שומע את הדברים ורואה את העגלות, מתוארת במפורש שריית רוח נבואה אצלו. בדרכו הוא זובח לאלהי אביו יצחק, ובחזיונות הלילה ניתנת לו הבטחה על הירידה למצרים, על היותו שם לעם רב ועל העלאתו.
explanation.en: Joseph promises to sustain his family in Goshen and emphasizes that he is speaking in his brothers’ language; Pharaoh adds wagons and an invitation to enjoy Egypt’s bounty. When Jacob hears the words and sees the wagons, the account explicitly describes a spirit of prophecy resting upon him. On the journey he sacrifices to the God of his father Isaac, and in visions of the night he receives a promise concerning the descent to Egypt, his becoming a numerous people there, and his being brought up.

dayTitle.he: משפחת יעקב בגושן והסדרי המזון והקרקע במצרים
dayTitle.en: Jacob’s family in Goshen and Egypt’s arrangements for food and land

explanation.he: רשימת בני המשפחה שומרת על שיוכם לאמהות ועל המניינים המפורשים, ואחריה מתוארים מפגש יוסף עם אביו והצגת המשפחה לפני פרעה. יעקב מברך את פרעה ומתאר את שנות מגוריו, ויוסף מיישב את המשפחה ומכלכל אותה. בהמשך מתחלפים כסף ומקנה בלחם, ואחר כך נקנים האנשים והקרקע לפרעה ונקבע חלקו ביבול, תוך החרגת אדמת הכמרים.
explanation.en: The family list preserves the maternal groupings and the stated totals, followed by Joseph’s reunion with his father and the family’s presentation before Pharaoh. Jacob blesses Pharaoh and describes his years of sojourning, while Joseph settles and sustains the family. Money and livestock are then exchanged for bread, after which the people and land are acquired for Pharaoh and his share of the produce is established, with the priests’ land excepted.

dayTitle.en: The two boards and the joining of the tribes

explanation.he: הנביא מצטווה לכתוב על שני לוחות את שמות קבוצות השבטים ולקרבם. התרגום מפרש את האות כאיחוד שבטי יוסף ויהודה לעם אחד. הלוחות נשארים ביד הנביא לעיני העם.
explanation.en: The prophet is commanded to write the tribal groupings on two boards and bring them together. The Targum explains the sign through the joining of the tribes of Joseph and Judah into one people. The boards remain in the prophet’s hand before the people’s eyes.

dayTitle.en: Gathering the people and one leadership

explanation.he: בני ישראל נקבצים מן העמים ונעשים לעם אחד תחת מלך אחד. ההבטחה כוללת טהרה מן העוונות והליכה בדינים ובקיומים. דוד נקרא במפורש עבד ה׳ ומלך, ולכל העם נזכר פרנס אחד.
explanation.en: The children of Israel are gathered from the peoples and made one people under one king. The promise includes purification from wrongdoing and walking according to judgments and ordinances. David is explicitly called the Divine servant and king, with one leader for the whole people.

dayTitle.en: The spring of life, love, and storing knowledge

explanation.he: הפה של הצדיק נמשל למבוע חיים והחכמה נמצאת בשפתי הנבון. שנאה מגרה ריב ואהבה מכסה סרחונות. החכמים אוצרים דעת, ואילו בפיו של השוטה מתקרבת הכליה.
explanation.en: The mouth of the righteous is compared to a spring of life, and wisdom is found on discerning lips. Hatred stirs quarrels while love covers offenses. The wise store knowledge, while destruction is near the fool’s mouth.

dayTitle.en: Possessions, deeds, discipline, and many words

explanation.he: הרכוש והמחסור מוצגים מול תוצאות מעשי הצדיק והרשע. שמירת המשמעת מתוארת כדרך חיים והעזיבה כתעייה. בסיום מודגשים הסכנה שבריבוי דברים והריסון שבשמירת השפתיים.
explanation.en: Possessions and need are set beside the consequences of righteous and wicked deeds. Keeping discipline is described as a path of life, and abandoning reproof as straying. The ending emphasizes sin amid many words and the discernment of restraining the lips.

dayTitle.en: The prophecy concerning גוֹג and the assembled camps

explanation.he: הנביא מקבל נבואה על גוג ועל המחנות הנלווים אליו. התיאור מפרט סוסים, פרשים, כלי מגן ושמות עמים ומקומות. השמות נשמרים כשמות שבנוסח העתיק, בלי שיוך למדינות זמננו.
explanation.en: The prophet receives a prophecy concerning גוֹג and the camps accompanying him. Horses, horsemen, armor, and names of peoples and places are specified. Those names remain names in the ancient text, without identification with present-day countries.

dayTitle.en: The lazy messenger, hope, and the way of God

explanation.he: השליח העצל נמשל לחומץ ולעשן המכבידים על החושים. יראת אלהים, תקוות הצדיקים ודרך אלהים נזכרות מול קיצור השנים, אובדן התקווה וכליית עושה העוול. הדברים נמסרים כלשון משלים ולא כאבחנה על אדם מסוים.
explanation.en: The lazy messenger is compared to vinegar and smoke that trouble the senses. Fear of God, righteous hope, and God’s way stand against shortened years, lost hope, and the destruction of wrongdoing. These remain sayings, not a diagnosis of a particular person.

dayTitle.he: לשון הצדיק, ברכת אלהים ויסוד בעולם
dayTitle.en: Righteous speech, God's blessing, and a foundation in the world

explanation.he: לשון הצדיק נמשלת לכסף נבחר ושפתי הצדיקים מפרנסות רבים, ואילו שוטים מתים בחסרון דעת. ברכת אלהים מעשירה ואין כאב נוסף עמה. בסיום הרשע נמשל לעלעל החולף, והצדיק מתואר כיסוד בעולם.
explanation.en: The righteous tongue is compared to choice silver, and righteous lips feed many, while fools die through lack of understanding. God's blessing enriches, with no pain added alongside it. At the end the wicked person passes like a whirlwind, while the righteous person is described as a foundation in the world.

dayTitle.en: Diligence, the remembrance of the righteous, and speech

explanation.he: המשלים מעמידים את עבודת הקיץ מול שינה בקציר ואת זיכרון הצדיק לברכה מול דעיכת שם הרשע. חכם הלב מקבל מצוה, וההולך בתמימות הולך בסעד. מי שדרכיו עקומות נודע; הרומז בעיניו גורם כאב, והעקום בשפתיו נלכד.
explanation.en: The sayings contrast summer work with sleep at harvest and the blessed remembrance of the righteous with the extinguishing of the wicked name. The wise-hearted receive a commandment, and those who walk in integrity go with support. One whose ways are crooked becomes known; one who signals with his eyes causes pain, and one who is crooked with his lips is caught.

dayTitle.he: מחשבת הביזה כנגד העם היושב לבטח
dayTitle.en: The plan of plunder against the people dwelling securely

explanation.he: גוג עתיד לעלות עם מחנותיו ועם עמים רבים כענן המכסה את הארץ. בתיאור הארץ נזכרים שיבה וקיבוץ מעמים רבים, והעם יושב לבטח בלי חומה, בריחים ודלתות. המחשבות העולות בלב גוג נקראות רעות: מטרתו לבוז שלל ולכנס את מחנותיו על החורבות שנושבו ועל העם שהצליח ברכושו.
explanation.en: גוג is to advance with his camps and many peoples like a cloud covering the land. The description of the land mentions return and gathering from many peoples, and the people dwell securely without a wall, bars or gates. The thoughts rising in גוג's heart are called evil: he intends to take plunder and spoil and assemble his camps against resettled ruins and a people who have prospered in property.

dayTitle.en: The land, the covenant of peace, and the Divine Presence

explanation.he: הישיבה בארץ שניתנה ליעקב מתוארת לדורות ולנצח, עם מלכות דוד וברית שלום. ה׳ מבטיח לברך את העם ולהרבותו, להציב את מקדשו בתוכו ולהשרות בו את שכינתו. העמים יכירו שה׳ מקדש את ישראל. בסיום נפתח דבר נבואה חדש.
explanation.en: Dwelling in the land given to Jacob is promised across generations and forever, with David's kingship and a covenant of peace. God promises to bless and increase the people, place His sanctuary among them, and cause His Divine Presence to dwell among them. The peoples will know that God sanctifies Israel. A new word of prophecy opens at the end.
